question: Which of the following officers managed stores and the supply of weapons like spears and swords during the Gupta period?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ranabhandagarika**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The officer known as the **Ranabhandagarika** during the Gupta period was responsible for managing the stores and the supply of weapons like spears and swords.
 
• This position held significant importance in the Gupta administration as it ensured the proper maintenance of weaponry for military operations and defense.
 
• The term "Ranabhandagarika" is derived from "Rana" (war) and "Bhandagarika" (storekeeper), clearly indicating their role in managing war supplies.
 
• Efficient administration of weapon storage and supply played a crucial role in maintaining the Gupta Empire's military strength and ensuring readiness for wars or invasions.
 
• The Gupta Empire had a well-organized administrative system, and the Ranabhandagarika was a key official associated with the military department.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sandhivigrahika**

 
 
• The Sandhivigrahika was an important officer in the Gupta administration, often referred to as the minister of peace and war.
 
• This officer was responsible for matters related to negotiations, treaties, and war strategies, acting as an intermediary in diplomatic discussions.
 
• The Sandhivigrahika played a vital role in maintaining foreign relations and ensuring the security of the Gupta Empire through strategic alliances.
 
 
 
• **Kumaramatya**
 
 
• Kumaramatyas were high-ranking officials in the Gupta administration who were typically appointed by the king to oversee various administrative and judicial functions.
 
• They were often members of the royal family or trusted nobles and held significant responsibilities in the governance of provinces and districts.
 
• The Kumaramatyas contributed to the efficient functioning of the central and provincial administration during the Gupta period.
 
 
 
• **Mahadandanayaka**
 
 
• The Mahadandanayaka was the chief judicial officer in the Gupta administration, equivalent to the modern-day chief justice.
 
• This officer was responsible for maintaining law and order, resolving disputes, and ensuring the implementation of judicial decisions.
 
• The Mahadandanayaka played a crucial role in upholding justice and the legal framework of the Gupta Empire.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Administration**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire (circa 320–550 CE) is known for its efficient administrative system, which was divided into central, provincial, district, and village levels.
 
• The empire had a well-organized military system, with specialized officials like the Ranabhandagarika for managing war supplies.
 
• The Gupta period is often referred to as the "Golden Age of India" due to its advancements in administration, culture, economy, and scientific achievements.
